subject: Follow-up: Long-context evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Long-context evals & next steps

Hey John,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — great to hear more about Acme's plans for multi-document conversation summarization across long customer interaction histories. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get a targeted evaluation running: 

Recap from our call:
- Primary goal: accurate, faithful summarization of multi-session customer support threads (some records >50k tokens once you concat attachments + transcripts).
- Key concerns: truncation behavior, hallucination risk when summarizing long context, latency for on-demand summaries, and cost per inference at scale.
- Data posture: most data is PII-stripped but remains sensitive; procurement may want Dedicated/Private deployment options.

What we'll evaluate (proposal):
1) Summarization fidelity on full concatenated context (no chunking) to measure truncation/fidelity.
2) Chunked & RAG-based summarization to compare info-preservation vs latency/cost.
3) Truncation stress test: very long tails (>50k tokens) to see where models degrade.

Immediate concrete items from Redwood (what I'll run next week unless you want to change):
- Baseline models: redwood-long-8b (32k/64k variant), redwood-extended-3b (long-window tuned).
- Quantization/Perf profiles: q4_hybrid for cost-aware runs; full fp16 for quality runs.
- Metric suite: ROUGE-L, Info-preservation checklist (manual eval samples), and hallucination-precision score from our eval harness.
- Acceptance criteria draft: ROUGE-L >= X (we'll share numbers after first run), hallucination rate < 5% on critical fields, summary completeness > 90% on priority prompts.

Attachments: I attached two files to seed the eval: acme_long_context_samples.jsonl (5 representative long-thread samples) and acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt set and rubric).

Questions for you / asks to unblock:
- Can you confirm a sample of 10-20 long threads we can use for the first pass? The attached files are placeholders; if you prefer we can pull directly from your S3 (you can share read-only link).
- Is Dedicated or Private deployment a requirement for the evals due to procurement? If yes, we'll scope a Dedicated evaluation (runs inside our reserved capacity) or propose a Private pilot.
- Any specific redlines from Legal re: data handling we should account for before we run the samples?

Proposed timeline:
- Start evals: week of Mar 8 (3-4 business days to run baselines and collect metrics).
- Share preliminary results + short demo: Mar 12-13.

Next steps I suggest now:
1) You confirm sample access and deployment preference (hosted/dedicated/private).
2) I'll queue the evals and share a concise results dashboard + draft acceptance criteria.
3) Follow-up sync after results (30 minutes) to align on model selection and rollout.

Links I'll reference in the report: redwood model catalog + eval dashboard (I'll share direct links in the results email).

If you’re good with this, I’ll start the baseline runs on Monday and loop in Rishi for the deeper performance configs.

Thanks,

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Long-context evals & next steps

Hi John — great, thanks. Attached and below are the baseline recommendations, rough cost direction, and links to the eval artifacts. I'll start the runs once you confirm sample access.

Recommended models & rationale:
- redwood-long-8b (64k variant): Best quality/cost tradeoff for long-window summarization. Tuned attention kernels for tokens >32k; expected to maintain coherence longer than vanilla weights.
- redwood-extended-3b: Lower cost alternative with reasonable summary quality on chunked+RAG pipelines. Good candidate for throughput-sensitive use cases.

Performance & truncation notes:
- For contexts >32k tokens we recommend testing both the 64k variant (redwood-long-8b) and a chunked RAG pipeline. Some degradation is expected beyond 64k on single-pass summarization; chunked RAG preserves higher info density at the cost of added latency.
- We'll run a truncation stress test that reports the token position where summary quality sharply drops (we'll surface a plot).

Cost (very rough estimate for the proposed 3-4 day eval run on 10-20 samples):
- Hosted (redwood API, baseline runs, q4 profiles): ~$800–$1,500 total (depends on sample length).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity/private pilot; includes infra/time): starting ~ $6k for a short pilot (VM/GPU time + engineering support).

Artifacts I attached/shared:
- acme_prompt_set_v1.txt — prompt templates and evaluation rubric.
- acme_long_context_samples.jsonl — 10 representative sample threads (sanitized).
- acme_long_eval_results_v1.csv — placeholder results format we'll populate after the run.

Important links (will appear in the final report):
- Eval dashboard (preview): https://console.redwood.ai/evals/acme-long-context-2026-03
- Model catalog entries: https://console.redwood.ai/models/redwood-long-8b and https://console.redwood.ai/models/redwood-extended-3b

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- ROUGE-L on priority prompts within 10% of the human reference baseline.
- Hallucination rate < 5% on critical customer attributes.
- Summary completeness > 90% on the rubric items for top-5 prompts.

Privacy/deployment options:
- Hosted evals: quick, lower friction, data sent to Redwood hosted inference. Suitable if sanitized samples are provided.
- Dedicated/Private: we can run inside your VPC or our Dedicated pool; procurement/legal will likely prefer this for production. We can scope a Private pilot if you prefer no data leaves your environment.

Proposed next steps:
1) John: share 10 sanitized samples (you mentioned EOD Tue).
2) Marissa/Rishi: run the three eval buckets (baseline single-pass, chunked+RAG, truncation stress).
3) Results + short demo: we'll aim to share dashboard and a 30-minute review the week of Mar 12.

If procurement wants a high-level SOW or a sketch of the Dedicated pilot costs, I can pull that together after we validate the results.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0112
